message.content: In lions, the most well‑known dominant genetic trait is the presence of a mane in adult males. The allele that encodes the development of a mane is dominant over the allele that results in a maneless phenotype. In other words, if a lion inherits one copy of the “mane” allele (from either parent), it will develop a mane; only when it inherits two copies of the recessive “no‑mane” allele does it remain maneless. This dominant allele is also responsible for the typical dark (black) coloration of the mane.
